Hi Lisa — thanks for the note, excited to help. Short answers up front: we can structure a private offer as usage-based (per-token/embedding) or as a blended seat+usage pilot depending on what you want to measure; and term lengths for private offers are flexible — pilots are commonly 3–6 months, production private offers are 12–24 months.

To do this efficiently, can you share: 1) an estimated monthly token/embedding volume or a target number of seats; 2) whether you need SOC2 / VPC/private deployment options for the pilot; and 3) the stakeholder approval chain (procurement, legal, security).

I'm looping in Marissa from Finance to confirm how we handle pricing cadence and any required internal approvals for private-offer activation. We'll put together a short options worksheet and a recommended buyer-approval map.

Best,
Alex Martinez

Hi all — quick finance note: the attached XLSX includes two pricing lanes — Pilot (3–6 months) and Production (12 or 24 months). For pilots we typically offer a discounted blended rate (seat + usage) with no upfront commitment; production private offers require a minimum commit to enable reserved capacity and volume discounts.

Important operational gating: to activate a private offer via AWS Marketplace we need a named buyer on the HubSpot deal and an internal activation approval (Finance + Marketplace Ops). If HealthWorks wants a 24-month term with deeper discounts, Finance will require a signed SOW or PO and a CFO or delegated signatory. For pilots under $50k ARR-equivalent we can often activate with procurement signoff only.

Alex — cc'ing Vanessa from Legal to surface any standard PO terms we should highlight (auto-renewal, termination windows).

Thanks,

Some context on approvals at HealthWorks: procurement will sign off for pilots under $40k; above that procurement + finance (FP&A) need to review; security (CISO) reviews any private deployment or if we need VPC/HSM integrations. Our preferred term for pilots is 6 months; production typically expects 12 months (we don't often do 24-months without exec approval).

Two clarifying asks: 1) For a 6-month pilot, can you include a one-time onboarding credit and a KPI-based conversion credit if we go to production? 2) If we request a 12-month production private offer, can pricing be pro-rated into our annual budget window (starts July 1)?

On the SOC2 / evidence side — procurement asked for a short SOC2 summary; can you include that when you send the private-offer paperwork?

Hi Lisa — thanks for laying out HealthWorks' approval thresholds. From a legal/terms perspective we recommend the following for simplicity and to minimize procurement friction:

- Pilot: 6 months, blended pilot rate, one-time onboarding credit (we typically cover first month up to $5k USD), KPI-based conversion credit (up to 10% credit applied to first production invoice if you meet agreed-upon success criteria).
- Production: default term 12 months with an option to extend to 24 months for an incremental discount schedule; 12-month offers can be pro-rated to a July 1 budget start if the PO references the fiscal period.
- Standard marketplace activation: procurement PO + named buyer + acceptance of standard AWS Marketplace seller terms. If you need private deployment (VPC or on-prem), security review (CISO) is required prior to activation and may add 2–4 weeks.

For the DocuSign/activation packet we will include the SOC2 summary and a short runbook describing onboarding and key contact points (CS, solutions engineering). If you want, we can draft a mutual action plan with milestones (kickoff, data sandbox, production readiness) and I can include target signatories for different dollar thresholds.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf
